label: copy-phase input v re-fed as 1st/2nd copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input is v and it is the first or second copied token (v was original token 0 or 1; recall_idx 1 or 2). Magnitude depends strongly on position: v as the first copied token (input right after <DEL>, orig(0)=v) gives near-max activation (~0.85-1.0 of max, 82% of mass); v as the second copied token (orig(1)=v) gives weak activation (~0.05-0.3). Almost no activation for v deeper in the copy (a handful of tiny ~0.02 activations at recall_idx 3). Never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter, never on v when it is the original-phase input, and never on any token other than v. Small false-positive set is mostly weak recall_idx 2 cases.

issues: Most of the label checks out. On the dev split, all activations are in the copy phase. 32364 of 32365 are on in_tok v (one is on r). Mass is 82% at recall_idx 1 and 18% at recall_idx 2, with 76 tiny activations at recall_idx 3 and nothing in the original or delimiter phases. Precision for v at recall_idx 1 is 1.000 (16980 predicted).

There is a systematic false-positive class the explanation does not mention: the second-token (recall_idx 2) case depends on sequence length. For v at recall_idx 2, dev precision is 0.016 at L=3 (450 predicted) and 0.64 at L=4 (2396 predicted). At L=5, 6 and 9 it is 1.000. So the feature almost never fires on a second copied v when L=3, the step that emits the last token. The roughly 1291 test false positives are almost all at L=3 and L=4. They are not 'mostly weak cases at recall_idx 2' scattered at random.

Within L=4, the misses I sampled did not separate cleanly by prev_tok (digits, vowels, ranges) or by next_out. Precision stayed between 0.58 and 0.69 in every split, so part of the L=4 behaviour is still unexplained.
The 66 missed activations hold 0.0% of the mass. They are all tiny (0.01-0.06) and sit on v at recall_idx 3 (orig(2)=v). That is consistent with the claim and is scattered noise.
Adding the length condition to the predicate improves test F1 from 0.979 to 0.985 (precision 0.973, recall 0.998, mass recall 1.000).
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input v re-fed as the 1st copied token (strong), or as the 2nd copied token (weak, only when L>=4, partial at L=4)

final_label: copy-phase input v re-fed as the 1st copied token (strong), or as the 2nd copied token (weak, only when L>=4, partial at L=4)
